We developed a whole-brain simultaneous functional near-infrared spectroscopy-electroencephalography (fNIRS-EEG) approach to capture fast temporal electrophysiological and spatially accurate hemodynamic signals during long-lag repetition learning. Thirty participants performed a semantic judgment task with words repeated across four runs with intervening items, modeling repetition demands central to reading instruction. A multimodal decoding framework integrating electrophysiological, hemodynamic, and cross-modal fNIRS-EEG correlation features was used to classify repetition-based learning. Repeated words showed response time reductions. EEG captured a frontal N400-range repetition-related negativity and attenuation of alpha-beta suppression, reflecting changes in recognition-related and post-recognition processing. fNIRS revealed left inferior frontal and superior temporal efficiency increases alongside right supramarginal activation, suggesting integrative processing. Multimodal classifiers outperformed unimodal classifiers, indicating that each modality captured complementary aspects of learning. Combining fNIRS and EEG with multimodal machine learning provides a richer characterization of repetition-based learning than either modality alone, establishing a framework for phenotyping language learning capacity and identifying neural markers of reading difficulties in pediatric populations.

papers.title: Chrononutritional regulation of metabolic homeostasis: intermittent fasting through gut microbiota, circadian rhythms, and autophagy.
papers.abstract: The global obesity epidemic has increased the burden of metabolic diseases. Dietary interventions are key to managing obesity and improving metabolic health. Intermittent fasting (IF) has emerged as a promising chrononutritional intervention that may modulate metabolic metabolic homeostasis through timed eating-fasting cycles. This review examines four main IF patterns:time-restricted feeding (TRF), alternate day fasting (ADF), the 5:2 fasting, and the 4:3 fasting, and evaluates their effects on body weight, glucose homeostasis, insulin sensitivity, and lipid profiles. Furthermore, it delineates the mechanistic pathways through which IF confers metabolic benefits beyond caloric restriction alone: (1) alleviating insulin resistance by enhancing the intestinal mucosal barrier and upregulating GLP-1 expression suppressing endotoxemia-related inflammation; (2) restoring circadian rhythmicity in the expression of metabolism-related genes to correct metabolic dysregulation; (3) increasing energy expenditure and lipid oxidation via short-chain fatty acid-mediated browning of white adipose tissue (WAT); and (4) enhancing cellular autophagy through activation of the SIRT3-AMPK-mTOR signaling pathway, thereby improving overall metabolic function. Evidence supports IF as a potentially effective alternative for obesity and metabolic disorders through chronobiological mechanisms. However, potential adverse effects like hypoglycemia and adherence challenges highlight the need for individualized approaches in clinical practice.

papers.title: Initiation of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy and Lifestyle Modifications for Morbid Obesity in a Patient With Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation, Severe Osteoarthritis, and Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: This case report describes a 57-year-old man with morbid obesity, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and severe knee osteoarthritis. We discuss the successful optimization of his metabolic and orthopedic risks through the initiation of a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist in conjunction with a structured lifestyle modification plan. This case demonstrates the measurable benefit of combining advanced pharmacotherapy with targeted behavioral interventions to manage complex, obesity-related comorbidities. Through the course of a 12-month monitoring period, this patient shifted his body mass index (BMI) from stage 2 to stage 1 obesity, moved his blood pressure to a healthier range, and achieved measurable improvements in his lipid profile.

papers.title: Chronic Kidney Disease-Associated Pruritus in Danish Dialysis Patients: A Cross-Sectional Multicenter Study of Prevalence, Disease Burden, and Current Treatment Practices.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus (CKD-aP) is rarely systematically assessed despite the potential negative impact on quality of life (QoL). This study investigated prevalence, disease burden, physician awareness, and treatment practices. Multicenter cross-sectional study using patient-reported outcome measures and a physician practice survey. Adult patients with chronic kidney failure requiring replacement therapy and nephrologists from 8 Danish hospitals. Kidney failure requiring replacement therapy and dialysis modality. CKD-aP prevalence (score, >4) and pruritus severity (range, 0-10) according to the Worst Itch Numeric Rating Scale (WI-NRS). QoL and skin distribution assessed with the 5-D itch scale (range, 5-25). Physician awareness and treatment practices (self-invented questionnaire). Descriptive statistics were used. We recruited 642 patients (∼25% of the Danish dialysis population): 83% receiving hemodialysis (HD), 13% receiving peritoneal dialysis, and 4% receiving home HD (HHD). The median WI-NRS score (IQR) was 0 (0-4). CKD-aP prevalence (95% CI) was 21% (18%-24%) (WI-NRS, >4). Moderate to very severe pruritus (WI-NRS, ≥4) was found in 25% (19%-32%). The median 5-D score (IQR) was 5 (5-10) (all patients). Peritoneal dialysis patients had significantly higher WI-NRS and 5-D scores than HD and HHD patients. Overall, the impact of CKD-aP on daily activities was minimal, but sleep disability (score, >1) was found in 20%. Sleep disability correlated significantly with higher WI-NRS scores. Based on 75 questionnaires (nephrologists/residents: 46/25), most physicians overestimated CKD-aP prevalence and favored dialysis, and fatty cream and phosphate-lowering treatment, rather than systemic treatment with gabapentinoids or difelikefalin. Single time-point estimate of CKD-aP and few HHD patients. No dermatologic evaluation was performed to exclude other pruritic conditions. About 1 of 5 to 1 of 4 dialysis patients had CKD-aP, which mainly impaired QoL via sleep disturbance. Physicians demonstrated adequate awareness, but treatment remained largely limited to dialysis and fatty cream. Simple patient-reported outcome measures facilitated systematic assessment.

papers.title: Longitudinal changes in resting-state EEG eyes-closed/open delta differentiation during an Antarctic expedition.
papers.abstract: Antarctic polar night brings extreme light deprivation, prolonged isolation and severe circadian disruption, yet longitudinal resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) signatures reflecting neurophysiological alterations in this harsh environment remain poorly characterized. In this exploratory longitudinal research, resting-state EEG recordings with eyes open (EO) and eyes closed (EC) were acquired from 16 Antarctic expeditioners at four mission stages: pre-departure, pre-polar-night, early post-polar-night, and austral summer. Linear mixed-effects models with false discovery rate correction were applied to analyze delta eyes-closed/open differentiation (the EC-EO delta log-power difference), delta sub-bands, aperiodic spectral features, entropy, EEG microstates and delta-band functional connectivity. The delta EC-EO difference exhibited consistent, progressively negative shifts in parietal, frontal, whole-brain and occipital regions across the expedition timeline, with the most pronounced shifts observed in recordings obtained during and after the polar-night period; this effect spanned all slow, mid and fast delta sub-bands. Secondary mild temporal variations were observed in aperiodic spectral metrics, occipital sample entropy and global delta connectivity, whereas EEG microstates displayed no significant longitudinal alterations. Collectively, the delta EC-EO difference emerges as a candidate EEG index of resting-state condition differentiation in the low-frequency range, pending validation in larger studies with synchronized behavioral, physiological, and environmental measures.

papers.title: Wild ginseng adventitious roots restore sleep homeostasis in sleep-deprived Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation is increasingly recognized as a major health concern and is associated with impaired physiological and neurological functions. Panax ginseng C. A. Mey. has long been used to improve sleep quality; however, the limited availability and long cultivation cycle of natural ginseng restrict its sustainable utilization. Wild ginseng adventitious roots (ADV), produced via plant tissue culture, provide a renewable source of bioactive ginsenosides, although their potential role in sleep regulation remains poorly understood. The sleep-promoting effects and safety of ADV were evaluated in a sleep deprivation-induced Drosophila melanogaster model. Sleep parameters, including total sleep duration, sleep latency, deep sleep, and sleep fragmentation, were assessed, together with addiction-like behavioral assays. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to investigate the underlying mechanisms. LC-MS/MS and bioactivity assays were conducted to identify and validate major active ginsenosides. ADV significantly improved sleep behavior in sleep-deprived flies, increasing total sleep duration and deep sleep while reducing sleep latency and sleep fragmentation, without inducing addiction-like behaviors. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that ADV modulated multiple sleep-related biological processes, particularly stress response pathway, as evidenced by altered expression of Hsp68, Hsp70Aa, Hsp70Ba, Hsp70Bb, and Hsp70Bbb. Combined with LC-MS/MS identification and biological activity comparison, ginsenosides Rc and F2 were preliminarily identified as the principal active metabolites. In the Drosophila melanogaster sleep-deprivation model, ADV treatment is associated with improvements in sleep-related behavioural parameters alongside altered expression of conserved stress-response-related biological processes. These findings support ADV as a sustainable source of bioactive ginsenosides, though the current experimental design cannot establish a strictly sleep-specific or causal mechanistic relationship.

papers.title: Acute differences in field-based physical performance between Ramadan-type fasting and non-fasting conditions in 10-11-year-old youth soccer players.
papers.abstract: Ramadan-type fasting involves prolonged abstinence from food and fluids and may influence physical performance, fatigue, hydration-related responses, and sleep. However, evidence regarding its acute effects on field-based performance in preadolescent soccer players remains limited. This study aimed to compare physical performance, physiological and perceptual responses, sleep duration, and body mass between fed and Ramadan-type fasted conditions in 10-11-year-old male youth soccer players. Fifteen male youth soccer players completed a within-subject repeated-measures design under two nutritional conditions: fed and Ramadan-type fasted. In the Ramadan-type fasted condition, participants abstained from food and fluid intake for approximately 14 h before testing, whereas in the fed condition testing was performed approximately 3.5-4 h after a standardized meal. Field-based performance was assessed using countermovement jump, 30-m sprint, Illinois agility test, and the Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Children's Test. Resting heart rate, pre-test subjective fatigue, post-Yo-Yo perceived exertion, sleep duration, and body mass were also recorded. Countermovement jump height, 30-m sprint time, and Illinois agility test time did not differ significantly between conditions. In contrast, Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Children's Test distance was significantly lower under the fasted condition compared with the fed condition. Resting heart rate, pre-test subjective fatigue, and post-Yo-Yo perceived exertion were significantly higher in the fasted condition, while sleep duration and body mass were significantly lower. These findings indicate that the Ramadan-type fasted condition was associated with lower intermittent endurance performance and greater perceptual strain, whereas no statistically significant differences were detected in isolated short-duration performance tasks in child soccer players. Coaches and practitioners should carefully monitor fatigue, perceived exertion, sleep, and recovery when planning intermittent endurance-oriented activities for children who voluntarily fast with parental approval.
papers.journal: Frontiers in sports and active living

papers.title: Pancreatic hamartoma presenting with sleep-related behavioral abnormalities due to neuroglycopenia: a case report.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic hamartoma (PH) is an exceedingly rare benign non-neoplastic lesion of the pancreas. Owing to its nonspecific clinical and radiological features, it is prone to misdiagnosis. Among its various subtypes, functionally active pancreatic hamartomas with distinct endocrine activity have only been sporadically reported in the literature as individual cases. We report the case of a 58-year-old female patient whose initial presentation was characterized by paroxysmal behavioral abnormalities during nocturnal sleep, manifesting as sudden agitation, arm-flinging, and purposeless stereotyped movements after sleep onset. During these episodes, the patient exhibited a confusional state with subsequent complete amnesia for the events, a clinical phenotype highly suggestive of REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) or frontal lobe epilepsy. In-hospital monitoring revealed refractory nocturnal hypoglycemia. Imaging studies identified a mass in the pancreatic tail, and the patient underwent laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy. Postoperative histopathological and immunohistochemical examination confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic hamartoma, composed predominantly of islet cells (approximately 90%) with associated islet cell tumor-like hyperplasia. Following surgery, the patient's nocturnal hypoglycemia and sleep-related behavioral abnormalities resolved completely.

papers.title: Smartphone-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia: A preliminary randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the first-line treatment for insomnia, but many individuals lack access. This study evaluated the preliminary efficacy of Hvil®, a 9-week, fully automated, smartphone delivered eCBT-I program, in reducing insomnia severity. Adults with insomnia (Insomnia Severity Index ≥10) were randomly assigned to an eCBT-I intervention via Hvil® or to a waitlist control group. The primary outcome of insomnia severity was assessed at baseline, weekly during the intervention, and post-intervention. Secondary outcomes included fatigue at baseline and post-intervention and sleep diary-based outcomes assessed daily during the study period. Mixed linear models (MLMs) based on the intent-to-treat sample were used to assess group differences over time. Moderating effects of demographic characteristics and adherence were explored. A total of 165 participants were randomized to the intervention (n = 83) or control group (n = 82). A significant group × time interaction was observed for insomnia severity (p < .001) favoring the intervention group, yielding a clinically meaningful effect size (Cohen's d = 0.66). Significant improvements were also noted in fatigue, sleep quality, time in bed, and nocturnal awakenings. Effect sizes for secondary outcomes ranged from 0.15 (total sleep time) to 1.06 (time in bed). Greater engagement with the Hvil® app was associated with larger reductions in insomnia severity (p < .001). Hvil®, an automated eCBT-I intervention, demonstrated significant efficacy in reducing insomnia severity among adults in the general population. While attrition was substantial, the results suggest its potential as a scalable, accessible intervention.

papers.title: Sleep quality and movement behaviors in school-aged children with overweight and obesity: a scoping review.
Healthy sleep pattern is associated with reduced risk of incident thyroid disease: a prospective cohort study from the UK Biobank.
papers.abstract: The longitudinal association between sleep behaviors and the incidence of various thyroid diseases remains unclear. This study aimed to prospectively investigate the association between a healthy sleep score and the risk of incident thyroid diseases using data from the UK Biobank. This prospective cohort study included 499, 084 adults aged 37-73 years from the UK Biobank. A healthy sleep score ranging from 0 to 5 was constructed based on five self-reported sleep behaviors: chronotype, sleep duration, insomnia, snoring, and daytime excessive sleepiness. Participants with missing information on sleep behaviors were excluded from the construction of the healthy sleep score. Incident outcomes included overall thyroid disease, hypothyroidism, nontoxic goiter, thyrotoxicosis, thyroiditis, thyroid cancer, and iodine deficiency-related diseases. After adjustment for multiple covariates, higher healthy sleep scores were dose-dependently associated with lower risks of overall thyroid disease, hypothyroidism, nontoxic goiter, and thyrotoxicosis. Compared with participants with poor sleep patterns (scores of 0-1), those with the healthiest sleep pattern (score of 5) had significantly lower risks of overall thyroid disease (24% [17%-31%]), hypothyroidism (25% [17%-32%]), nontoxic goiter (26% [7%-41%]), and thyrotoxicosis (32% [15%-45%]). Among the five sleep components, the absence of frequent daytime excessive sleepiness showed a particularly evident association with lower risks of thyroid disease. Furthermore, interaction analyses suggested that the inverse association between the healthy sleep score and the risk of overall thyroid disease may vary by sex, BMI, and diabetes status, with more pronounced associations observed among women, individuals with obesity, and those without diabetes. Higher healthy sleep scores were associated with lower risks of incident overall thyroid disease, hypothyroidism, nontoxic goiter, and thyrotoxicosis. Among the individual sleep components, the absence of frequent daytime excessive sleepiness showed the strongest association with a lower risk of thyroid disease.

papers.title: Adsorptive Removal of 1,2-Dichloroethane Using Novel Oleogel Adsorbents: Synthesis Strategy and Adsorption Mechanism Insight.
papers.abstract: 1,2-Dichloroethane (DCE) is a widely used, highly volatile, and lipophilic industrial solvent. As a chlorine-containing volatile organic compound (VOC), DCE emissions pose significant risks to human health and the ecological environment. Adsorption is considered an economical and environmentally friendly method for eliminating air pollutants. In this study, novel Oleogel adsorbents were prepared via self-assembly and polymeric cross-linking mechanisms, using 12-hydroxystearic acid (12-HSA) and ethyl cellulose (EC) as gelators, and rapeseed oil (RO) and dioctyl adipate (DOA) as base oils. A series of oleogels were fabricated by varying the type and dosage of gelators, and their structures, physicochemical properties, and DCE adsorption performance were systematically characterized. The DCE adsorption behavior and mechanism were investigated through dynamic adsorption experiments, multimodel kinetic fitting, and spectral analysis at multiple temperatures. The results showed that the 10 wt % 12-HSA/DOA Oleogel achieved a DCE adsorption capacity of 154.4 mg g-1 at 25 °C and reached 201.9 mg g-1 at 15 °C, which is comparable to those of previously reported adsorbents. Characterization and adsorption experiments demonstrated that the adsorbent exhibited a stable three-dimensional crystalline architecture, excellent oil retention (up to 98% after centrifugation), and favorable thermal stability below 150 °C. Meanwhile, DCE adsorption on Oleogel adsorbents involves significant intermolecular interactions (e.g., dipole-dipole and hydrogen bonding) rather than a purely physical process, and their surface is enriched with exposed functional groups, such as carbonyl and carboxyl groups. Further analysis indicated that the base oil was the dominant factor governing DCE adsorption performance, and the gelator type was the decisive factor influencing crystal morphology development. Notably, the contact angle of samples prepared from ethyl cellulose and dioctyl adipate reached 95.6°, suggesting potential for use in high-humidity environments.

papers.title: Density Spectral Array Patterns During Total Intravenous Anesthesia with Intravenous Lidocaine for Craniotomy: An Illustrative Two-Case Series.
papers.abstract: Intravenous lidocaine is used as an adjuvant to total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA). To our knowledge, density spectral array (DSA) patterns during intravenous lidocaine administration in propofol-remifentanil TIVA for craniotomy have rarely been described. We present two illustrative cases for educational and hypothesis-generating purposes. Two adults underwent craniotomy for tumor resection (left cerebellopontine angle, Case 1; suprasellar, Case 2) with effect-site target-controlled infusion of propofol (Schnider model) and remifentanil (Minto model) and a bilateral scalp block. After a 1.5 mg/kg bolus, lidocaine was infused at 1.5 mg/kg/hour (Case 1) or 2 mg/kg/hour (Case 2) and stopped 30 minutes before the end of surgery. Frontal bispectral index (BIS) and DSA were recorded throughout and interpreted qualitatively at the bedside and offline. In Case 1, an alpha-delta pattern persisted during maintenance, including at the lowest targets used (propofol 1.8 mcg/mL, remifentanil 2.5 ng/mL; BIS 39-45). In Case 2, the DSA showed more pronounced delta dominance, attenuated alpha and beta activity, and intermittent burst suppression, which persisted when propofol was reduced to 1.5 mcg/mL. In both patients, transient beta-power increases were temporally associated with surgical stimulation; electromyographic contribution could not be excluded. No hemodynamic instability or adverse effect attributable to lidocaine was observed. This two-patient illustrative case series demonstrates differing DSA patterns during propofol-remifentanil TIVA with two intravenous lidocaine infusion regimens. Because the observations come from different patients with multiple clinical and anesthetic confounders, no dose-response relationship or causal effect of lidocaine can be established. These hypothesis-generating observations require evaluation in controlled studies.

papers.title: DIalysis Symptom COntrol-Pruritus Outcome Trial (DISCO-POT): A Multicenter Randomized Blinded Placebo Controlled Crossover Trial.
papers.abstract: Uremic pruritus affects up to 50% of patients with kidney failure and negatively impacts quality of life. Itch often persists and remains insufficiently controlled despite standard of care treatments. We evaluated the effects of nabilone, a synthetic cannabinoid, in patients with kidney failure receiving dialysis who had symptoms of chronic itch. Placebo-controlled randomized crossover trial. Adults ≥25 years old receiving maintenance hemodialysis at least twice weekly or peritoneal dialysis daily with at least moderate itch. Participants were randomly allocated to a first treatment period of either oral nabilone (0.5 mg daily for 1 week then twice a day for 3 weeks) or an identical placebo regimen. After a 2-week washout period, participants received whichever regimen they did not receive in the first treatment period. The primary outcome was the difference in worst visual analog score (0 to 100 mm) for itch over the last 24 hours in each treatment period. Of 14 participants randomized, all were receiving hemodialysis. The worst visual analog score for the nabilone compared to the placebo was 4.88 mm (95% CI, -3.61 to 13.38, P = 0.28), indicating worse itch with nabilone. The study was not able to detect any differences in nabilone compared with placebo in other measures of itch, sleep, quality of life, or adverse events. Underpowered for secondary outcomes and to detect carryover effects, conservative nabilone dosing, short duration and a limited sample. We were unable to detect if nabilone had any effects on uremic pruritus compared with placebo.

papers.title: Digital behavior therapy for insomnia in the general population: secondary analysis of the multi-arm RESiLIENT trial with active comparators.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is common and often coexists with depression and anxiety. Digital delivery can expand access, yet few trials have compared insomnia-focused behavioral interventions with strong active controls under standardized conditions. To examine whether a smartphone-delivered behavior therapy for insomnia (BI) improves insomnia more than a mood-focused behavioral activation (BA) module or a health-information (HI) comparator, and whether combining BI with BA (BA+BI) adds benefit. We conducted a secondary analysis of the multi-arm RESiLIENT randomized controlled trial among adults from the general population with elevated insomnia (Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) ≥8). Participants were assigned to BI, BA+BI, BA, or HI, each self-guided over six weeks. The primary outcome was ISI change at weeks 6 and 26, analyzed using mixed-effects models. Depressive (PHQ-9) and anxiety (GAD-7) symptoms were secondary outcomes. Analyses followed a modified intention-to-treat approach (≥1 post-baseline assessment). At week 6, BI reduced insomnia severity more than HI (ES: -0.43, CI: -0.58 to -0.28) and BA (ES: -0.26, CI: -0.42 to -0.11); BA also exceeded HI (ES: -0.16, CI: -0.32 to -0.01). Adding BA to BI gave no benefit over BI alone (vs HI, ES: -0.30, CI: -0.45 to -0.14). BI reduced depressive (ES: -0.44, CI: -0.59 to -0.29) and anxiety symptoms (ES: -0.27, CI: -0.42 to -0.12) more than HI, and matched BA (each ES: 0.05, CI: -0.10 to 0.20). At week 26, ISI differences persisted but PHQ-9 and GAD-7 differences attenuated. This exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis associated a focused smartphone-delivered sleep intervention with durable improvements in insomnia severity and mood. Replication in independent samples, and confirmation in trials recruiting participants with elevated insomnia, is required before recommendation at scale.

papers.title: Musculoskeletal impact of hybrid work in Indian IT professionals: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated a shift to work-from-home (WFH) across the information technology (IT) sector, often without adequate ergonomic workstations, raising concerns about musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) from prolonged sedentary postures. This study assessed MSD prevalence among IT professionals in Pune, India, and its associations with work hours, ergonomic setup, sleep, and exercise. We conducted a cross-sectional study among IT professionals at selected software companies in Pune, India (May-September 2022), following STROBE guidelines. An online questionnaire (Google Forms) was completed by 280 employees; 214 (76.4%) also underwent on-site physical examination and formed the final analytic sample. Participants aged 18-60 years gave written informed consent; those with prior musculoskeletal surgery or autoimmune disorders were excluded. Examination included BMI and the Straight Leg Raise (SLR) test. Chi-square tests and Pearson correlations were analysed using SPSS v26.0. Most participants were male (86.9%), mean age 45.16 years. Current MSD pain affected 54.2% (95% CI 47.5-60.9%), predominantly lower back (68.2%; 95% CI 60.1-75.4%) and neck (41.4%). Chronic pain (>1 year) was present in 52.3%, and 40.2% reported worsening since the pandemic. Daily working hours was the only significant predictor (chi-square = 9.379, df = 3, p = 0.025); those working 12-14 h/day had the highest prevalence (63.3%). Ergonomic-setup absence, sleep <6 h, exercise, age, and BMI were not significantly associated, though sleep approached significance (p = 0.056). The SLR test was positive in 29.0%. MSDs are prevalent among hybrid-era IT professionals in Pune, where extended working hours was the sole significant predictor; ergonomic deficiency and short sleep showed non-significant trends. Reducing daily work hours and improving home-workstation ergonomics are the most evidence-supported intervention targets.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical orthopaedics and trauma

papers.title: Targeting glial modulation: molecular mechanisms of Polygonatum in neurological disorders.
papers.abstract: Neurological disorders arise from interconnected pathological processes, including oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired proteostasis, synaptic injury and blood brain barrier disruption. Increasing evidence indicates that glial cells are not passive bystanders in these diseases, but central regulators of neuroimmune balance, metabolic support, myelin integrity and tissue repair. Polygonatum spp., a traditional medicinal and edible plant, contains diverse bioactive constituents, including polysaccharides, steroidal saponins and flavonoids, which exhibit multi-target neuroprotective activities. In this Review, we summarize current evidence linking Polygonatum and its active compounds to the modulation of glial function and neuronal survival. Polygonatum polysaccharides appear to suppress microglial overactivation, attenuate TLR4/NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammatory signalling, restore redox homeostasis through NRF2-related pathways, and reduce lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis. In parallel, Polygonatum-derived compounds may support mitochondrial function, protein homeostasis, synaptic plasticity and neurotransmitter balance, thereby improving pathological outcomes in models of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, cerebral ischaemia, depression and sleep disturbance. Evidence for direct effects on oligodendrocytes, astrocytes, oligodendrocyte precursor cells and the neurovascular unit remains limited but suggests an important area for future investigation. Standardized botanical sources, extraction procedures, pharmacokinetic analyses and high-quality clinical studies will be essential to define the therapeutic potential of Polygonatum-based interventions for neurological diseases.

papers.title: Knowledge and Prevalence of Bruxism and Its Association With Stress Among Clinical-Year Dental and Medical Students at the University of Ghana.
papers.abstract: Bruxism is a repetitive jaw-muscle activity characterised by clenching or grinding of the teeth and/or by bracing or thrusting of the mandible. Current international consensus regards it as a motor behaviour rather than a disorder, and one that may act as a risk factor for tooth wear and temporomandibular disorders; psychosocial stress is among its most consistently reported associated factors. Clinical-year dental and medical students face intense academic and clinical pressure that may predispose them to both stress and bruxism, yet no published Ghanaian data on this relationship previously existed. A cross-sectional study was conducted among clinical-year (4th-6th year) dental and medical students at the University of Ghana, Korle Bu campus. A stratified sample of 291 students, proportionally allocated by course and clinical year, completed a self-administered online questionnaire comprising a 12-point bruxism knowledge module, a 10-item bruxism symptom screening module and the 30-item Perceived Stress Questionnaire (PSQ). Prevalence estimates are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Associations were examined using chi-square tests, multivariable linear regression, and Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficients, at α = 0.05. Participants had a mean age of 23.6 ± 2.3 years; 55.0% were male, and 85.2% were medical students. Only 19.6% (95% CI: 15.4%-24.5%) demonstrated good knowledge of bruxism, with dental students (48.8% vs. 14.5%, p < 0.001) and final-year students (p = 0.04) significantly more knowledgeable. Self-reported awareness of awake bruxism was 36.1% (95% CI: 30.8%-41.7%) and of sleep bruxism 14.4% (95% CI: 10.9%-18.9%); on the composite 10-item screening score, 9.3% (95% CI: 6.5%-13.2%) of students met the threshold for subject-based (self-reported) bruxism, with no significant socio-demographic differences. High perceived stress was recorded in 8.9% (95% CI: 6.2%-12.8%) of students. Stress correlated significantly, though weakly, with bruxism symptom scores (Pearson's r = 0.25, 95% CI: 0.14-0.35, p < 0.001; Spearman's ρ = 0.212, p = 0.0003 (p < 0.001). Knowledge of bruxism is markedly poorer among medical than dental students, and among junior compared with final-year trainees. Self-reported bruxism symptoms are common despite a low rate of high perceived stress, and stress shows a modest but significant positive association with bruxism. Curricular bruxism education for medical students and proactive stress-reduction initiatives are warranted.

papers.title: Association of stress-related genetic risk and lifestyle factors with BMI in Korean adults.
papers.abstract: Genetic susceptibility to stress may influence behavioral and metabolic responses involved in dietary choices and body weight regulation. While previous studies have focused on individual genetic variants related to dietary intake and obesity risk, a polygenic approach integrating multiple stress-related single nucleotide polymorphisms may better capture overall genetic susceptibility to stress. This study examined the relationship among stress-related polygenic risk, dietary intake, serum metabolite profiles, and body weight, and determined whether this relationship could be influenced by sleep duration and physical activity (PA). This study included 100 disease-free participants with a body mass index (BMI) of 18.5 to 25.0 kg/m2. The genetic scores for stress (GSstress) were determined using 4 genes: DRD2 rs1800497, COMT rs4680, BDNF rs6265, and HTR2C rs3813929. Participants were classified into 4 categories: Low GSstress (n = 29), Normal GSstress (n = 16), Alert GSstress (n = 36), and Risk GSstress (n = 19). Anthropometric measurements, dietary intake, PA, sleep duration, serum cortisol, and serum metabolite levels were evaluated. Serum cortisol concentration was significantly higher in the Risk GSstress group than in the Low GSstress and Alert GSstress groups. Participants with higher risk for stress consumed significantly higher sugar-sweetened beverages (SSB) than those at low risk. Additionally, there was a significant interaction effect between GSstress and sleep duration in relation to BMI (P = 0.041), with a positive association found only in individuals with short sleep duration (< 6 h/day). This study demonstrated that individuals with a higher genetic risk for stress exhibited elevated cortisol levels and were associated with greater SSB intake and higher BMI. This relationship was more pronounced in those with insufficient sleep, emphasizing the importance of lifestyle factors in mitigating the effect of genetic stress risk on body weight. Clinical Research Information Service Identifier: KCT0004650.

papers.title: Self-reported prescription medication use and polypharmacy following physical combat injury in the UK: the ADVANCE cohort study.
papers.abstract: The consequences of serious physical traumatic injury may require pharmacological intervention, however long-term use and polypharmacy can increase risk of morbidity/mortality. This study aims to describe prescription medication use in a cohort of UK Armed Forces personnel who sustained physical combat injuries during the Afghanistan conflict (injured group) compared to demographically similar personnel without such injuries (uninjured group) a median of 11 years post injury. One thousand and fifty one participants of the ADVANCE cohort (injured group n = 526 uninjured group n = 525), including individuals with (n = 141) and without (n = 384) limb loss or with (n = 226) and without (n = 300) deployment-related Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI), reported medication use during a clinical interview. Overall incidence of prescribing any medication, specific anatomical/therapeutic classes (e.g., Central Nervous System (CNS), psychotropic or analgesic) and medications with pain or mental health indications were investigated. General (≥5 medications), CNS (≥5), psychotropic (≥2) and analgesic (≥2) polypharmacy was also investigated. Compared to the uninjured group, the injured group reported a greater prevalence of prescription medication use (17.8% vs. 29.7%), including medications acting on the CNS (8.0% vs. 17.2%), psychotropics (6.3% vs. 11.8%) and analgesics (2.2% vs. 8.6%). Prevalence of polypharmacy was very low in the cohort (0%-4.4%). Incidence Rate Ratios (IRR) and 95% confidence intervals indicated that injured personnel were currently using on average over twice as many prescription medications as those in the uninjured group (IRR 2.15 (1.66, 2.92)), including medications acting on the CNS (IRR 2.67 (1.77, 4.08)), and psychotropics (IRR 2.03 (1.27, 3.25)). Similar elevations were present in those injured with and without limb loss and especially elevated in those with deployment-related TBI. Use of psychotropics amongst personnel injured with limb loss were predominantly for non-mental health indications (e.g., sleep, pain). Pharmacological intervention is not uncommon amongst UK Armed Forces personnel who sustained serious physical injuries, but the prevalence of polypharmacy is low. Effective prescribing practices should ensure optimal recovery whilst minimising the risk of adverse events.

papers.title: TCANet: a temporal convolutional attention network for EEG-based cognitive load assessment in simulated flight tasks.
papers.abstract: Effective cognitive load assessment facilitates optimized task allocation and plays a critical role in evaluating human performance in domains such as flight safety monitoring and human-computer interaction. Electroencephalography (EEG) has been extensively employed in cognitive load research owing to its high temporal resolution, non-invasiveness, and accessibility. However, EEG signals exhibit substantial variability across individuals and task conditions, making it challenging to extract stable and discriminative features related to cognitive load. Accordingly, we propose TCANet, a Temporal Convolutional Attention Network designed to learn discriminative EEG representations for cognitive load classification in simulated flight tasks. The proposed network integrates multi-branch temporal convolutions, dilated convolutions, and attention mechanisms to model temporal, spatial, and channel-wise EEG information while reducing redundant feature responses. We designed an EEG-based cognitive load classification paradigm involving two pilot-simulated flight scenarios. A total of 20 participants were recruited, with 15 participants completing the turning task and 5 participants completing the landing task. TCANet achieved average classification accuracies of 90.15% and 81.52% on the turning-task and landing-task datasets, respectively. The turning-task dataset served as the primary evaluation dataset, whereas the landing-task dataset provided a supplementary evaluation under a different simulated flight task. Statistical analyses of frequency-band power indicated task-condition-related variations in EEG spectral activity. Neurophysiological variations, particularly in the Theta and Alpha bands, and feature representation analyses further provided interpretable evidence regarding cognitive-load-related EEG patterns and the discriminative representations learned by TCANet.

papers.title: From community diagnosis to policy dialogue: co-creating childhood obesity prevention strategies in rural and urban Portugal.
papers.abstract: Promoting healthy lifestyles from early childhood is central to balanced development and the prevention of health problems throughout life. The European HEALTH4EUKids project examines a participatory process of community diagnosis, co-creation into local policies for child health promotion and childhood obesity prevention in two Portuguese territories with distinct rural and urban profiles. A cross-sectional observational study was conducted within a mixed-methods action-research framework. The study provides an exploratory assessment of children's wellbeing indicators and contextual differences, without permitting causal inference. Participants included 202 primary-school pupils (mean age = 7.43 ± 1.14 years) and 54 community adults (mean age = 48.76 ± 11.51 years), alongside stakeholders from health, community, and local decision-making sectors. Data included a questionnaire adapted from the 2022 Health Behavior in School-aged Children (HBSC) protocol, KIDSCREEN-10, the Living Healthy Tool (LHT) which was translated and culturally adapted for the Portuguese context, satisfaction questionnaires and focus groups. LHT-student version was administered exclusively in Alter do Chão. Quantitative and qualitative data were analyzed using SPSS v.28.0 and thematic analysis supported by MAXQDA. Descriptive analyses indicated that 57% of pupils reported irritability or bad mood and 46.7% reported nervousness, while quality of life and sleep were generally favorably rated. Regarding nutritional status, 66% had age-adjusted BMI within the reference range, whereas 36% reported not engaging in regular physical activity. Frequent screen use and exposure to violence during leisure time were also identified as concerns. Community LHT responses indicated differences between municipalities in perceptions of school meals, safety, and access to public services. Focus groups highlighted priorities concerning physical activity, school food environments, and coordination between schools, families, and the community. The findings indicate context-specific strengths and areas for further attention in child health and wellbeing. Quality of life, sleep patterns, and certain family health practices were generally favorable. Conversely, challenges were identified regarding physical activity, screen time, and psychological symptoms, as well as less favorable assessments of school meal quality, community safety, access to services, and opportunities for active leisure.

papers.title: Seven-day Accelerometer-derived Wrist Activity after Acute Stroke Stratified by Hemiparesis Severity: A Prospective Observational Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: This hypothesis-driven prospective pilot study characterized 7-day trajectories of bilateral wrist activity after acute stroke by baseline Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) severity. We hypothesized that mild impairment would be associated with greater paretic-side activity and more symmetric activity, whereas bilateral balance would change little despite clinical improvement. Patients who began rehabilitation within 3 days after stroke wore bilateral wrist accelerometers for 7 days. Exploratory strata were mild (FMA-UE >45) and severe (≤45), based on an inflection point of 45.3 reported for subacute stroke. Daily vector magnitude (VM) and magnitude ratio [MR = log10(paretic VM/non-paretic VM)] were analyzed using sex-adjusted linear mixed-effects models with participant random intercepts. Unannotated walking, care, therapy, and sleep were included; indices therefore represented overall inpatient wrist acceleration. Of 32 enrolled patients, 24 completed monitoring (mild impairment, n = 16; severe impairment, n = 8). At day 1, the severe group had lower paretic VM [β = -468,257 counts/day; 95% confidence interval (CI) -826,564 to -109,949; P = 0.010] and MR (β = -0.348; 95% CI -0.515 to -0.181; P <0.001) than the mild group. In the mild reference group, day coefficients were positive for non-paretic VM (β = 46,589; P <0.001) and paretic VM (β = 34,801; P = 0.002). Group-by-day interactions were nonsignificant, and MR showed no significant day effect. FMA-UE and Action Research Arm Test scores increased in both groups. Wrist activity and bilateral balance differed by baseline severity. MR showed no significant temporal change despite improved clinical motor scores. Bilateral wrist accelerometry may complement clinical assessment but reflects overall wrist acceleration rather than purposeful upper-limb use.

papers.title: Multimodal assessment of NIBS-induced adaptive plasticity in aging prefrontal networks: ERP and cognitive evidence.
papers.abstract: Non-invasive brain stimulation may enhance age-sensitive executive functions by modulating task-engaged prefrontal networks, but behavioral effects remain heterogeneous and their physiological specificity is poorly understood. This pre-post study examined neuropsychological and electrophysiological responses to cognitive training paired with active or sham transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Thirty-three older adults were randomly assigned to active tDCS plus cognitive training, sham tDCS plus cognitive training, or wait-list control. Training groups completed 24 sessions across 8 weeks. Before and after intervention, participants underwent neuropsychological assessment and EEG recording during a Stroop-like task; N2 amplitude and latency were extracted at F3, Fz, and F4. Linear mixed-effects models tested Group × Time effects. Significant interactions emerged for non-verbal executive functions and associative fluency, with improvements confined to the active-tDCS group. Other cognitive measures improved over time without group-specific effects. Active tDCS selectively increased N2 amplitude in correspondence to the stimulated site, whereas no comparable change occurred after sham stimulation or in controls. These findings suggest that repeated right-prefrontal tDCS may specifically support higher-order executive functions and induce selective modulation near the stimulation site. Physiological measures may help clarify the anatomical and functional specificity of NIBS-related modulation.

papers.title: Decoding morality through EEG with ML: rigour, risks, and the road ahead.
papers.abstract: The quest to decode morality through electroencephalography (EEG) with machine learning (ML) is as much about confronting the risks of opaque algorithms as it is about harnessing their scientific promise. This systematic review synthesises 17 empirical studies published between 2018 and 2025 that employed ML or deep learning (DL) approaches to EEG data within moral cognition paradigms. Following PRISMA guidelines, studies were identified across four electronic databases and categorised into eight experimental paradigms spanning three thematic branches: Evaluation, Emotion, and Prosociality. The Ultimatum Game was the most frequently applied paradigm (n = 6), while classical ML approaches dominated methodological choices, accounting for 65% of the included studies. Despite the growing interest in DL, interpretability was inconsistently addressed, with Explainable Artificial Intelligence methods applied in only one of the six DL studies and in just two of the 17 included studies overall. This review highlights three pressing methodological gaps: the need for multimodal fusion to capture richer neural signals, the integration of transfer learning to enhance generalisability, and the adoption of standardised interpretability reporting to ensure transparency. We argue that ML offers a scientifically rigorous pathway for advancing EEG-based moral cognition research, but only when models are robustly validated and their outputs rendered explainable. Without these safeguards, the promise of decoding morality risks being undermined by opaque algorithms and methodological blind spots. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s11571-026-10559-4.

papers.title: Longitudinal white matter network reorganization after rTMS in first-episode schizophrenia: associations with sleep improvement.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are highly prevalent in first-episode schizophrenia and are associated with poor clinical and functional outcomes. Although repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has shown therapeutic potential for insomnia and schizophrenia, its efficacy for sleep disturbances in first-episode schizophrenia remains insufficiently characterized, and the underlying white matter network mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to determine whether active rTMS improves sleep quality compared with sham stimulation and whether longitudinal white matter network reorganization is associated with treatment-related sleep improvement. One hundred patients with first-episode schizophrenia were included in the final analysis and randomly assigned to receive active rTMS or sham stimulation over an 8-week intervention period. Subjective sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and objective sleep parameters were measured using wrist actigraphy. Diffusion tensor imaging was acquired at baseline and after treatment to construct individual white matter structural networks. Graph-theoretical metrics, nodal efficiency, and rich-club organization were examined. Linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate group-by-time interaction effects, and correlation analyses were performed to examine associations between network changes and sleep improvement. Compared with sham stimulation, active rTMS produced greater improvements in subjective and objective sleep outcomes, including reduced PSQI scores, increased sleep efficiency, and decreased wake after sleep onset and sleep latency. Active rTMS was also associated with greater longitudinal increases in global efficiency, local efficiency, clustering coefficient, and nodal efficiency in prefrontal, default-mode, temporal, and salience-related regions. Rich-club connectivity increased more strongly after active rTMS than after sham stimulation, whereas feeder connectivity, normalized rich-club coefficient, and local connectivity did not show significant group-by-time interaction effects after FDR correction. In the active rTMS group, increases in rich-club connectivity were positively associated with improvements in actigraphy-derived sleep efficiency (r = 0.43, P = 0.002). Active rTMS improved sleep quality more effectively than sham stimulation in patients with first-episode schizophrenia and was accompanied by longitudinal changes in DTI-derived white matter network organization. The association between increased rich-club connectivity and improved sleep efficiency suggests that hub-related network reorganization may represent a network-level correlate of rTMS-related sleep improvement.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomics and metabolomics reveal Cry1-associated hepatic alterations and plasma essential fatty acids as biomarkers of residual circadian disruption post-sepsis.
papers.abstract: Sepsis disrupts circadian rhythm, leaving lasting molecular traces and circadian insensitivity to jet lag even after acute phase recovery. However, the core mechanism and biomarkers of residual circadian dysfunction post-sepsis remain unclear, which hinders targeted interventions. Male mice were subjected to non-lethal LPS injection, and after 7 days of recovery, liver transcriptomics and plasma metabolomics were integrated. Behavioral, physiological, and molecular analyses were performed, with statistical tests including DESeq2, Student's t-test, MetaCycle, and ROC curve analysis. Significant transcriptomic alterations were observed, most prominently at Zeitgeber time 21. Linoleic acid (LA) and alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) were identified as sampling-time-independent candidate biomarkers associated with post-sepsis circadian disruption. Exogenous supplementation of these two fatty acids shortened male mice's rhythm re-entrainment period. This study identifies a hypothesized Cry1-essential fatty acid axis potentially contributing to post-sepsis circadian dysfunction based on multi-omics associations, providing novel biomarkers and a metabolic intervention strategy for detecting and treating circadian rhythm disorders in sepsis survivors.

papers.title: Clinical features and outcomes of atezolizumab-associated encephalitis.
papers.abstract: To explore the clinical characteristics of atezolizumab-associated encephalitis and to provide clinical evidence for diagnosis and treatment. Clinical reports on atezolizumab-associated encephalitis published before June 30, 2026 were collected for retrospective analysis by searching Chinese and English databases. A total of 39 cases of encephalitis were included, with a median age of 60 years (33, 78). The median time of symptom onset was 14 days (2, 420) after the initial administration. Fever (53.8%), confusion (51.3%) and headache (28.2%) were the main complaints of the patients. Cerebrospinal fluid examination showed elevated white blood cell count and protein, with median values of 27 cells/μL (1, 553) and 133mg/dL (27.1, 815), respectively. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed T2 fluid-attenuated inversion recovery hyperintensities in half of the patients. Electroencephalogram showed display epileptiform discharges (26.7%) and slow waves (40.0%). After discontinuation of atezolizumab and initiation of targeted treatment, 97.4% of patients achieved symptomatic improvement or recovery, while 2.6% died of encephalitis-related complications. Patients with atezolizumab-associated encephalitis were predominantly middle-aged and elderly, with fever, confusion and headache as the major manifestations. Clinicians should be alert to the potential risk of encephalitis during atezolizumab treatment. Most patients obtained symptom relief or clinical recovery following atezolizumab discontinuation and treatment; only a few succumbed to severe encephalitis-related complications.

papers.title: Clinical, functional, and quality-of-life characteristics of women with comorbid fibromyalgia and irritable bowel syndrome and their associations with FIQR scores.
papers.abstract: Fibromyalgia (FM) and irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) frequently co-occur, sharing pathophysiological mechanisms such as central sensitization and gut-brain axis dysregulation. Given that exercise is a first-line non-pharmacological intervention for FM, detailed baseline characterization may inform future exercise-based research. This study aimed to describe the physical, functional, symptomatic, and quality-of-life profile of women with FM+IBS comorbidity in relation to FM severity, assessed continuously and, secondarily, categorically using the Revised Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQR). This cross-sectional observational study, conducted at IRCCS "Saverio de Bellis" (Castellana Grotte, Bari, Italy), enrolled 33 women (mean age 47.7 ± 8.6 years) diagnosed with FM (2016 ACR criteria) and IBS (Rome IV criteria). Participants were stratified into three groups by FIQR score: Remission/Mild (n=7), Moderate (n=13), and High Severity (n=13). FIQR total score was analyzed as a continuous exposure using Spearman correlations with bootstrapped 95% CIs as the primary analysis; the three-group stratification was retained as a secondary, exploratory presentation. Assessments included pain (VAS), tender points, gastrointestinal symptoms (IBS-SSS), kinesiophobia (TSK), sleep quality (PSQI), physical activity (IPAQ), functional fitness tests, and quality of life (SF-36). Perceived pain showed the strongest association with FIQR severity (Spearman's rho=0.57, p<0.001), with values nearly doubling in the High Severity versus Remission/Mild stratum. Physical activity level (IPAQ; exact p=0.021) differed significantly across FIQR strata, with greater inactivity in the Moderate group. Lower-limb functional strength/endurance, handgrip strength, six-minute walk distance, kinesiophobia, and SF-36 Mental Component Summary were all significantly associated with continuous FIQR (all p<0.05); the Sit-to-Stand difference across categorical strata, significant under standard ANOVA (p=0.048), lost significance under Welch's ANOVA (p=0.148) and Kruskal-Wallis testing (p=0.072). Gastrointestinal burden remained elevated across all groups, with no clear association with FIQR severity (rho=0.29, p=0.097). Sleep quality and SF-36 scores were markedly impaired regardless of FIQR class. In this exploratory sample, greater FM severity was primarily associated with increased pain and reduced lower-limb functional capacity, while gastrointestinal burden remained consistently elevated across the severity spectrum. These descriptive, hypothesis-generating findings may help guide the design of future, adequately powered studies addressing pain threshold, functional capacity, and gastrointestinal tolerance in exercise management of FM+IBS.

papers.title: Prevalence of burnout syndrome and associated factors among nurses in Mogadishu, Somalia: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Burnout is a major occupational health concern among nurses, with important implications for workforce well-being, quality of care, and patient safety. However, evidence on its prevalence and associated factors among nurses in Somalia remains limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of burnout syndrome and identify associated factors among nurses in Mogadishu, Somalia. A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted between 1 January and 28 February 2026 across five hospitals in Mogadishu. A total of 292 nurses completed an online self-administered questionnaire. Burnout was assessed using the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS) and defined as high emotional exhaustion (≥27), high depersonalization (≥13), and low personal accomplishment (≤31). Associations with sociodemographic, occupational, and psychosocial factors were examined using logistic regression. Results are presented as adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. A total of 292 nurses participated, of whom 18.2% (95% CI: 13.9-23.1) met the study definition of burnout. In the sociodemographic/occupational model, burnout was associated with mixed shift schedules, longer service duration, chronic illness, and high workload, with the strongest association observed among nurses with >10 years of service (AOR = 3.63, 95% CI: 1.40-9.40). In the psychosocial model, depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, poor sleep quality, and job dissatisfaction were associated with burnout, with depressive symptoms showing the strongest association (AOR = 5.85, 95% CI: 2.61-13.14). Nearly one in five nurses met the study definition of burnout, with several occupational, psychological, and health-related factors associated with burnout. These findings may inform workplace strategies to support nurses' well-being, while longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted categorization of interictal abnormalities in adult long-term electroencephalographic monitoring: Comparable diagnostic accuracy with marked efficiency gain.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) classifies routine electroencephalograms (EEGs) with expert-level accuracy, but interpretation of long-term EEG monitoring (LTM) remains reliant on time-intensive visual review. We evaluated whether autoSCORE, a clinically approved implementation of SCORE-AI integrated into an EEG reader, achieves expert-level diagnostic accuracy for LTM interpretation and whether expert-supervised use reduces review time versus conventional analysis. A fixed-and-frozen AI model was tested on an independent single-center dataset of 78 adult patient LTM recordings (52 normal, 26 abnormal), with epilepsy monitoring unit discharge diagnosis as the external reference standard. The AI model was benchmarked against two expert panels (three readers each); Panel 1 reviewed autoSCORE EEG detections (hybrid approach), and Panel 2 interpreted full recordings (conventional approach). Diagnostic accuracy and time to diagnostic decision were assessed for fully automated, hybrid, and conventional approaches. Interrater reliability (Gwet's AC1) was evaluated for hybrid and conventional interpretation. Interrater reliability was significantly higher for hybrid than conventional approach (AC1 = .81, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .73-.89 vs. AC1 = .43, 95% CI = .32-.53; p < .001). Review time was markedly reduced (median [interquartile range (IQR)] = 2.2 [.5-4.3] vs. 52.4 [33.2-62.9] min, mean [95% CI] = 2.9 [2.5-3.2] vs. 50.8 [46.5-55.2] min, p < .001), a 95.8% median reduction (IQR = 95.6-96.3). Diagnostic performance comparisons were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Holm-Bonferroni procedure across all 63 tests. The hybrid approach showed significantly higher sensitivity than conventional interpretation (.88, 95% CI = .77-.97 vs. .69, 95% CI = .57-.81; adjusted p = .006). Its numerically higher diagnostic accuracy versus conventional interpretation (.75, 95% CI = .66-.83 vs. .68, 95% CI = .61-.74) was nonsignificant after correction (adjusted p > .99). Hybrid approach diagnostic accuracy was significantly greater than fully automated analysis (.75, 95% CI = .66-.83 vs. .55, 95% CI = .44-.65; adjusted p < .001). Expert oversight of AI-assisted categorization of interictal epileptiform and nonepileptiform EEG abnormalities improves interrater reliability and efficiency, increases diagnostic sensitivity versus conventional interpretation, and increases diagnostic accuracy versus fully automated analysis in adult LTM.

papers.title: Multimodal modeling of the ictal onset zone in refractory insular epilepsy and seizure outcome of magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial therapy: A pediatric single-center retrospective study.
papers.abstract: This study was undertaken to evaluate seizure outcomes after magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy (MRgLITT) in children with insular epilepsy and to assess how the extent of ablation overlaps with multimodal definitions of the ictal onset zone (IOZ). We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including consecutive pediatric patients treated with MRgLITT for insular epilepsy. All patients underwent presurgical evaluation including electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and stereo-EEG (SEEG) were performed in negative-MRI cases. Epileptic zone was identified by visual analysis of SEEG recording. Postablation contrast-enhancing volumes were manually segmented and coregistered with IOZ estimates derived from Multi-centre Epilepsy Lesion Detection (MELD) MRI analysis, FDG-PET voxel-based analysis, and the Epileptogenicity Index, when available. Spatial concordance between modalities was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients, and the proportion of each IOZ modality encompassed within the ablation volume was correlated with postoperative seizure outcomes (International League Against Epilepsy classification). Eight children (median age = 10.4 years, range = 2.3-17) were included, with a median postoperative follow-up of 38 months. Two patients had insular tumors, and both achieved seizure freedom after complete ablation. Among the six MRI-negative patients, FDG-PET revealed insular hypometabolism in four, MELD detected a median of one insular cluster (range 1-3), and SEEG identified focal insular ictal activity in three cases. Overall, four negative-MRI patients achieved seizure freedom: three after MRgLITT alone and one after MRgLITT combined with frontal opercular resection. One transient postoperative aphasia was observed. Intermodality spatial concordance was low across all comparisons. A greater proportion of FDG-PET hypometabolism included in the ablation volume was associated with better seizure outcomes (p = .012). MRgLITT is an effective and safe treatment option for focal insular epilepsy in children, either as standalone therapy or in a combined approach. Optimal outcome depends on accurate preoperative delineation of the IOZ and its complete ablation.

papers.title: Habitual Diet, Gut Microbiome Dysbiosis, and α-Synucleinopathy Conversion in Isolated Rapid Eye Movement (REM) Sleep Behavior Disorder.
papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence indicates that habitual diet, including plant-based dietary patterns, is associated with neurodegenerative α-synucleinopathy risk. However, the role of diet and its correlation with the gut microbiome in prodromal α-synucleinopathy, specifically among patients with isolated rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), remains unclear. To evaluate dietary patterns, their interplay with gut microbial dysbiosis, and longitudinal effects on neurodegenerative progression in iRBD patients. We recruited 287 iRBD patients and 208 age- and sex-matched controls. Plant-based diet indices (PDIs) were derived from food frequency questionnaires. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed in 456 subjects for diet-microbiome analyses. After a median follow-up of 4.2 years, 45 (15.7%) iRBD patients converted to α-synucleinopathies. Cox proportional hazards models assessed the associations between diet and neurodegenerative outcomes. We found that iRBD patients exhibited lower healthful PDIs (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 0.48 [0.29-0.80], P = 0.005) but higher consumption of unhealthful plant-based foods (refined grains, sweets, and sweeteners). Diet-microbiome interaction analysis identified dietary associations for 84.3% of iRBD-related gut microbes, including co-occurrence between healthful PDI and Clostridium sp. AF20-17LB. Longitudinally, four dietary factors and five iRBD-related microbes were associated with neurodegenerative outcomes; specifically, higher coffee consumption was linked to a lower risk of progression to α-synucleinopathy (aHR [95% CI]: 0.30 [0.11-0.78], P = 0.01). Furthermore, mediation analyses indicated that the iRBD-enriched species Ruthenibacterium lactatiformans mediated the association between unhealthful PDI and dementia-first conversion. Habitual diet in iRBD is associated with gut microbiome dysbiosis and predicts neurodegenerative progression. These findings highlight diet-microbiome interactions as modifiable targets for intervention in prodromal α-synucleinopathy. © 2026 The Author(s).
